title: "Experimental genomics & epigenomics"
subtitle: "What each assay measures—and which biological claims it supports"
---

## Design experiments around the inference

Assays become more powerful when students understand the relationship between their physical measurement and the biological quantity of interest. An ATAC-seq peak, for example, measures transposase-accessible DNA, not a direct enhancer–gene interaction or a guarantee of transcriptional activity.

### Chromatin measurements

- **Accessibility:** ATAC-seq and single-cell ATAC-seq; fragment length structure, TSS enrichment, sample quality and background.
- **Protein–DNA association:** ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag; antibody specificity, controls, fragment recovery and peak caller assumptions.
- **DNA modification:** bisulfite-based approaches, oxidative/hydroxymethylation strategies and direct long-read signal interpretation.
- **3D architecture:** Hi-C, targeted contact assays, insulation, compartments, loops and the impact of sequencing resolution.

### Experimental design studio

Learners select an assay for a biological hypothesis, articulate what they cannot measure directly, design appropriate positive/negative controls and state what orthogonal evidence would make the result persuasive.
